response.text:
## I need one figure: how many years of backend engineering experience do you have?

The summary has no dates, durations, or role timeline, so I can't state or calculate a number. I won't estimate one, because a guessed figure on an application is a misrepresentation you'd have to defend in an interview or background check.

## What it costs to leave it out

- **You may fail the screen outright.** "8 years" is listed as *Required*. Applicant tracking systems and recruiters often filter on an explicit number. With no number, the summary doesn't show you meet the bar, so it can be rejected before anyone reads the rest.
- **Reviewers will assume the worst.** If a candidate omits years when the posting asks for them, many readers conclude the candidate falls short.
- **Your strong evidence gets less weight.** The 40,000 orders/day settlement pipeline signals seniority, but scale evidence supports a years claim. It doesn't replace one.

## Draft, ready once you give me the number

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services, most recently a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Prior work spans payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

- **If X is 8 or more:** I'll insert it as is. It meets the requirement directly.
- **If X is under 8:** I'll still state it truthfully and reframe the summary around depth, scale, and ownership to make the strongest honest case. If you have adjacent experience that counts as backend work (e.g., data pipelines or infrastructure), list it and I'll help you decide whether to include it.
